requirements.requirement: The same recognition module can have a different physical and functional job after reformatting.
A soluble assembly has no intracellular receptor tail; a membrane CAR is a receptor on a living cell.
The CAR example connects external recognition through a spacer and membrane-spanning segment to intracellular signalling.
Contact between opposed cell surfaces constrains reach and geometry; the receptor does not itself traverse both cells.
A soluble assembled protein needs appropriate folding, stability, distribution and useful action under its intended conditions.
Spacer context, receptor expression and clustering are separate requirements of the assembled CAR format.
Clustering can cause antigen-independent signalling in particular CAR constructs; this is not a claim that all binders cluster.
Isolated affinity or one architecture does not establish universally better activity, safety or efficacy.
The complete intended format needs testing; an isolated binder result is not proven portable performance.
The repeated teal recognition shape and orange target hold identity constant while the drawn physical context changes.
Shapes and dimensions are schematic, not atomic structures, biological scale or measured quantities.
Panel order, direction arrows and the signalling label explain a format contrast, not an efficacy hierarchy or measured response.

scope: Three complete prompt/provenance/review bodies; two associated already-classified SVGs and the later parent plus original-to-later exact diff are context. No new ordinary-lesson coverage.
